newsitem.title: USA: Judge sends Waldholtz to jail for drug exam. [CORRECTED 22:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Judge sends Waldholtz to jail for drug exam. [CORRECTED 22:00 GMT]

text.p: A judge ordered Joseph Waldholtz, ex-husband of Utah Republican Representative Enid Greene, to be jailed Thursday and examined by doctors after he admitted to using heroin, bouncing checks and stealing from his parents and a friend.
"I realise the impact of my behaviour," Waldholtz said at a hearing before U.S. District Judge Norma Holloway Johnson. "I've learned a great deal about a disease called addiction."

"There was a time when Joseph Waldholtz was an honest and honourable person," the heavy-set defendant said in a brief plea asking for help in continuing his drug rehabilitation programme and for bipolar disorder, or manic-depression.

Waldholtz acknowledged he was addicted to heroin and painkillers, saying he had entered a drug treatment programme at St. Francis Hospital in Pittsburgh, and admitted numerous other misdeeds since his guilty plea in June to charges of bank, election and tax fraud. He is awaiting sentencing.

Holloway rejected Chief Public Defender A.J. Kramer's plea not to send Waldholtz to the District of Columbia jail because of "the greater availability of drugs in the D.C. jail than any other places" and sent him there for a medical examination. She said she would then decide where to keep him until his sentencing.
His former wife, a rising star in the Republican Party, divorced him earlier this year after he disappeared suddenly amid a swirl of allegations of political and financial misdeeds.
(Corrects time of divorce to this year, from last year)

Assistant U.S. Attorney Craig Iscoe outlined in court Waldholtz's use of a gram a day of heroin, how he forged his dentist father's signature to obtain painkillers, stole checks from his stepmother and wrote $39,600 in checks on an account in which he kept an average balance of $60.

Waldholtz stole credit cards from his father, Harvey, and a friend and used them for unauthorised purchases. He stole his friend's Mastercard from her purse while she was being treated by his father, Iscoe said.
Harvey Waldholtz and his wife kicked him out of their Squirrel Hill, Pennsylvania, home earlier this month and changed the locks.

When told of the charges Wednesday, Chuck Roistacher, an attorney representing Greene, said, "Nothing he does really surprises us in terms of victimising individuals or family members. It appears he is incapable of not victimising family members, those who love him. We are surprised about the heroin allegations, but when you think about it, probably we shouldn't be."

In court, Kramer maintained the FBI had known about Waldholtz's addiction since the 1980s and asked the judge to consider sending him to a nearby Arlington County, Virginia, jail or a federal treatment facility in North Carolina where he could receive help for his addiction.
Waldholtz pleaded guilty to four charges in June, including filing false federal reports on contributions to Greene's 1994 campaign for Congress. He was the Utah congresswoman's campaign treasurer.

He pleaded guilty to failing to report campaign contributions, making false statements to the federal election agency, causing his then-wife to file a false tax return in 1993 and bank fraud for a check-kiting scheme.
Under federal sentencing guidelines, the 33-year-old Waldholtz could get 18 to 24 months in prison.
At the June hearing, Judge Johnson released him on his personal bond, told him to reside with his parents, set travel restrictions and ordered him not to commit any new crimes.
Greene has maintained that Waldholtz duped her but she decided not to seek re-election in November.
Greene, who won office as a champion of family values, got a divorce on June 5, the same day that Waldholtz pleaded guilty, and has sole custody of their year-old daughter.
Prosecutor Iscoe said Waldholtz told a friend that he needed her American Express card to buy his daughter a birthday present and then proceeded to spend $550 on himself.
